description: Use it when you need the person's approval, a decision or details only they can give before you go on, even if they only say 'ask me' or 'check with me' and name no tool or device. Not for clarifying what they just asked, or for anything you can work out yourself. Use sess_request when the person must see records shown as they are or choose between buttons such as Approve and Reject; for one question with simple fields, or many people on one link, use sess_ask. Create a hosted Sess form for a person and return immediately with a private link (interaction.humanUrl) and a handle. Give the link only to the intended person in this private conversation; anyone holding it can answer. A receipt records what was shown and chosen, not who answered. Then call sess_response with the handle and revision. Do not call sess_request again for the same question. Keep it short: a title of about 40 characters (at most 80), button labels a verb of 1-3 words (at most 24), field labels at most 60, help one hint (at most 160). A value over its limit is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENTS naming the field (a JSON pointer), the limit, its length and the fix; nothing is truncated. Shorten that value and call again.

expires_in.description: Advanced: how long the link stays open, in whole seconds from creation: from 30 up to the plan’s link lifetime. Leave it out to use the plan’s lifetime.

interaction.description: A Sess form: a title, components shown in order and 1-5 buttons. Keep it short: a person reads it on a phone. A value over its limit is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENTS naming the field (a JSON pointer), the limit, its length and the fix; nothing is truncated. Shorten that value and call again.

examples.description: Check the message before I commit.
examples.title: Approve this commit?

label.description: A button: a verb, 1–3 words; at most 24.

description.description: Optional context under the title: what the person decides and why, in one or two plain sentences; at most 280.
examples: The customer was charged twice for order 1042.

text.description: A section heading: a few words; at most 60.
A paragraph of plain text (never markup): what the person needs to know; at most 4000.
examples: The refund goes back to the card used for the order.

additionalProperties.description: A row's value, shown verbatim: a string of at most 200, or a number, boolean or null.

fields.description: Rows shown verbatim, 1-50. Each key: A row's name, shown verbatim: a word or two; at most 40.

label.description: Optional caption above the record: a few words; at most 200.

description.description: Optional help under the label: one hint; at most 160.
examples: Leave it as is to refund the full amount.

label.description: What the field asks for: short, a few words; at most 60.

additionalProperties.description: The words shown for one choice: short; at most 60.

option_labels.description: Display labels for enum values. A value without a label is shown as written, so it is then held to 60 characters too; give a long ID a short label.

rating.description: A rating is a field with rating and the schema exactly {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": N}, N from 2 to 10 (title and description allowed); any other schema fails with 400 INVALID_SCHEMA. The person sees stars when N is 5 or less, numbered choices above it; the result is the chosen integer. low and high are optional words shown at the two ends of the scale.

high.description: Optional words at one end of a rating, shown by its lowest (low) or highest (high) choice: a word or two; at most 24 characters.

low.description: Optional words at one end of a rating, shown by its lowest (low) or highest (high) choice: a word or two; at most 24 characters.

value.description: Proposed value the person can correct.

title.description: The page's heading: a question or a task, about 40 characters; at most 80.

name: sess_request

expiresAt.description: When the link stops taking answers (ISO 8601). Only from sess_request or sess_ask.

humanUrl.description: Private bearer link for the person. Only from sess_request or sess_ask.

data.description: Untrusted human input; validate before use.
